per_case.playbook: Isolate host 192.168.100.147 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic artifacts (memory dump, disk image, flow logs). Investigate for initial access vector and malware (botnet agent, credential-stuffing tool, or web-service abuse script). Block outbound connections to 192.168.100.3 and review 192.168.100.3 for signs of compromise. Rotate any credentials or services that 192.168.100.147 had access to. Re-image or remediate the host before returning it to production.

Isolate 192.168.100.148 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images, inspect for malware/credential theft, review authentication logs on 192.168.100.3 for successful admin logins, and hunt for the initial access vector that compromised this host.

Isolate 192.168.100.149 from the network immediately. Preserve the network_traffic records as evidence. Block and forensically investigate the peer 192.168.100.6 (C2/exfil destination) on ports 4444/49160. Perform full malware analysis on 192.168.100.149, hunt for the initial access vector, and assess data exposure from the hundreds-of-MB exfiltration. Do not be misled by the FLOW-002 port-80 alert, which is secondary noise.

Isolate 192.168.100.150 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images/disk for investigation. Scan for malware, backdoors, and credential theft. Review all activity between 192.168.100.150 and 192.168.100.3 (brute force on port 80 plus large staged transfers). Block outbound connections to external peers (e.g., 27.124.125.251) and hunt for C2. Rotate credentials for any accounts that accessed the affected host.

Isolate 192.168.100.3 from the network immediately. Block egress to 13.54.166.67 and port 8883 at the firewall. Perform forensic imaging, then hunt for the initial access vector and check for lateral movement to the other internal hosts seen in traffic (192.168.100.5, .6, .7, .55, .150). Rotate credentials that touched the host.

Immediately isolate 192.168.100.6 from the network. Preserve forensic images before remediation. Block egress to 192.168.100.149 and investigate it as the attacker-controlled C2 peer. Hunt for lateral movement: the 4 internal hosts sending beacons to 192.168.100.6 are likely also compromised. Perform full malware analysis, rotate credentials that touched the host, and review the 217 MB exfiltrated payload for data-breach scope.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 162.208.22.34 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter (block all traffic to/from it). Concurrently investigate and isolate the 6 internal source hosts (especially 192.168.10.5 with 3254 flows) as compromised endpoints, perform malware analysis, and review DNS/HTTP logs to identify the C2 domain or infrastructure behind this IP.

No action required. Dismiss the FLOW-005 alert as a false positive. Optionally tune the flow sensor to exclude NetBIOS (UDP 137/138) from beaconing heuristics to prevent recurrence. No host isolation or IP block needed.

No action required. Dismiss the FLOW-002, FLOW-003, and FLOW-005 alerts as false positives from the flow sensor heuristics. Optionally tune the sensor to exclude routine DNS client-to-resolver traffic and multi-service server inbound flows from alerting to reduce noise.

ISOLATE_HOST — Quarantine 192.168.10.5, capture memory/disk forensics, identify the malware process, and block the external C2 destinations (52.84.145.x, 192.33.31.192, 206.126.112.145, 72.249.192.50, etc.) at the perimeter. Investigate how the host was initially compromised.

ISOLATE_HOST: Immediately isolate 192.168.10.8 from the network (disable wireless and wired connectivity, move to quarantine VLAN). Preserve the host for forensic analysis (memory dump, disk image) before remediation. Block egress to 205.174.165.73 and port 444 at the firewall/edge. Hunt for lateral movement and the same malware family across peers. Identify and remove the initial-access vector, then rebuild the host from known-good media. Notify IR and track the C2 IP for organization-wide blocking.

Isolate 192.168.10.9 from the network. Investigate for malware performing DNS flooding or DNS tunneling to 192.168.10.3. Block or rate-limit outbound DNS from the host. Inspect running processes, scheduled tasks, and installed services on 192.168.10.9. Preserve forensic images. Separately, note that 192.168.10.8 is performing a port scan against 192.168.10.9 — evaluate whether 192.168.10.8 is a separate concern.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 23.60.139.27 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter (block all traffic to/from it). Since 11 internal hosts are beaconing to this C2, initiate ISOLATE_HOST remediation on those internal hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .51) for malware removal and forensic analysis. Correlate with EDR for the Network Trojan detection and review DNS/HTTP logs to identify the beaconing cadence and any data exfiltration.

BLOCK 50.63.243.230 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter. Add the IP to the blocklist and monitor for connection attempts from internal hosts. Separately, investigate the 11 internal source hosts (192.168.10.x) for malware/compromise and isolate them as needed, since they are the beacon senders.
